title: Annotatio VI §.V close (2b–c): against mandate; shut from Saints’ communion — stop before §.VI
pass_a_gloss: (b) Against this they appropriate Christ’s Mandate of the Holy Supper: For they are among those not proving themselves and not discerning Christ’s body, to whom certainly the benefit — i.e. Christ’s body — will not be communicated as reward of their disobedience. (c) Excluded for the time from the Communion of Saintly humans, Therefore much more from communion of Christ’s flesh — to be referred not to external communion with Weigelians and Schwenckfeldians, but to internal with the Orthodox — by which communion, belonging to all and only the faithful, as by a certain common yet spiritual bond and glue, they are united spiritually both with Christ and among themselves and cohere united.
pass_b_english: (2b) They stand against the Supper mandate — not proving themselves, not discerning the body — so Christ’s body is not given as prize for that disobedience.

(2c) Shut for now from the Saints’ human communion, they are shut much more from communion of Christ’s flesh — the Orthodox’s inward bond, not Weigelian/Schwenckfeldian externalism — uniting the faithful with Christ and each other. Stop §.V before §.VI.
source_text: (b) Contra, Mandatum Christi, Cœnæ S. appropriant: Sunt enim inter non probantes semet, corpusque Christi non discernentes, quibus certè beneficium i. e. corpus Christi, in inobedientiæ suæ præmium, haud communicabitur. (c) Communione Sanctorum hominum tantisper exclusi, Ergo multò magis communione carnis Christi, non ad externam, cum Weigelianis & Swenckfeldianis, sed internam, cum Orthodoxis, Communionem, referenda, cujusque communione, omnibus & solis fidelibus competente, ceu communi quodam, spirituali tamen, vinculo glutineque, spiritualiter, tam cum Christo, quam inter se, uniuntur & uniti cohærent.
